electrobun.detail: Electrobun 2.0.5 macOS CEF launches renderer processes with --no-sandbox. Its sandbox attribute disables RPC; it is not the Chromium OS sandbox.

methodology: Production-built Svelte assets; unsigned development desktop runtimes; no Vite dev server or HMR.
One app at a time. One excluded warmup per app, then alternating Electron/Electrobun run order.

CEF disables occluded-window backgrounding by default. Electron receives the matching --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows flag so desktop overlap cannot suspend animation frames. Other background defaults are retained.
Startup: OS spawn to interactive new-tab DOM plus two animation frames, observed over direct page CDP (25 ms discovery polling). Not cold disk-cache startup or physical screen presentation.
Same no-store HTTP fixture: 300 rows, no external assets, network requests, fonts, or public websites.

Electron gets a temporary user-data directory; Electrobun gets a unique storage partition. Electrobun still uses its shared CEF root/UI cache. OS caches are warm; this is not full-profile cold-start parity.

RSS is summed across the detached OS process group, including launcher, backend, GPU, storage, network and renderer helpers. Shared pages can be counted more than once; this is not private memory/physical footprint.
Idle CPU uses deltas in cumulative process-group CPU time over 2 seconds (1 second after tab close); 100% equals one CPU core. Very small differences are noisy.
Page JS and DOM timings use performance.now inside the same fixture, with one excluded JS workload warmup. DOM metric includes forced layout, not GPU presentation.

Tab switching: BrowserApi command through two requestAnimationFrame callbacks in the selected content page, including CDP discovery/transport. This is a responsiveness proxy, not input-to-photon latency.

UI feature tests invoke real DOM form/button handlers or BrowserApi and use CDP to inspect content. Native OS menus/clipboard, live window resizing, DRM, extensions, downloads and session restore are not verified.
These are the two prototype implementations on this host, not a framework-wide speed or security guarantee. Chromium versions and implementation architecture are recorded.

Feature checks were re-run after adding an explicit native-target teardown wait between checks. Initial check outcomes are retained in featureVerification.initialChecks; all ten performance trials and app artifacts are unchanged.

featureVerification.reason: Feature isolation now waits for previous native CDP targets to disappear. The earlier tab-state timeout attached to a previous test target during asynchronous CEF teardown. Initial checks are retained below; performance trials and app artifacts are unchanged.

methodology: Official HTTPS BrowserBench pages, full default workloads: Speedometer 3.1 (ten iterations), JetStream 3.0 (every default subtest), MotionMark 1.3.2 (all eight 30-second tests, automatic frame-rate detection). No shortened tests, custom suite filters, iteration overrides, or GPU/backend flags.

Each full pass uses a new app process and a fresh browsing profile/partition. 3 passes per app/suite, with alternating app order in the planned schedule. Resumed retries fill missing slots later; per-pass timestamps preserve the actual chronology. Suite-internal warmups are retained; no separate full-pass warmup in this measurement loop. A 10-second gap separates full passes. Separate full-workload adapter validation passes may precede the recorded comparison.

Same pinned Electron snapshot and Electrobun + CEF prototype as the local benchmark, optimized Svelte assets inside unsigned development desktop runtimes. Artifact hashes and actual Chromium versions are recorded.

CEF disables occluded-window backgrounding by default; Electron receives the matching flag. Other browser/runtime defaults are retained. No headless mode or emulated viewport. Native app activation, Page.bringToFront and native tab selection are used before starting each test, with a normal page-margin click if needed to restore content focus; document focus and visible state are required before start.

Default viewport is 1280 × 750 content pixels; actual viewport, screen, device scale, focus and visibility are recorded for each pass. MotionMark comparisons are withheld when detected target frame rates differ, viewport/scale differs, or a page becomes hidden.

Completion callbacks/events are observed without changing workloads, score calculation or benchmark settings. A CDP binding signals completion; the runner does not poll the renderer while a benchmark is running. Data serialization and screenshots happen after completion.

Scores are the suite's official overall scores; higher is better. The report shows median, every full-pass score and sample counts. JetStream's displayed score is rounded by its own UI; full per-subtest results are preserved.

OS caches are warm. Electron uses a temporary full profile; Electrobun uses a unique named persistent tab partition but retains its CEF root/UI cache. Page resources come from the public HTTPS site, so network/cache conditions are not fully controlled.

This is a normal desktop session, not a thermally controlled lab run. Power source, system load and browser versions are recorded. Other applications are not closed, and system power/refresh settings are not changed. Caffeinate keeps the display/system awake only while the runner is alive.
These are measurements of the two prototype implementations on this Mac. They do not establish a framework-wide performance ranking, feature parity, or production browser security.

MotionMark starts only after its controller has finished frame-rate calibration. Dashboard, system and final option frame rates must agree. Invalid/interrupted attempts are retained separately and excluded from summaries; --resume revalidates stored raw results before reusing completed passes.
